CruiseMapper currently has no ship schedule for Port Almeirim (Brazil Amazon)

Almeirim is an Amazon River cruise port and the northernmost municipality in Brazil's Para State. The town covers a total area of approx 73 km2 (28 mi2) and has a population of around 30,000.

Almeirim is located approx 483 km (300 ml) up the Amazon River from the Atlantic ocean, and halfway between Santarem and Belem.

The municipality encompasses a large part (95%) of the Maicuru Biological Reserve, covering a total area of approx 11518 km2 (4447 ml2). Serra do Areao Airport is in Monte Dourado district - approx 73 km (45 ml) away from the city.

Among the largest ever cruise ships that have stopped in Almeirim Brazil is the Phoenix Reisen ship Albatros (on January 16, 2018) as part of an Around The World Cruise itinerary roundtrip from Hamburg Germany. The smaller itinerary segment (Jan 13-31, 20-days long) that included Almeirim started in Manaus and ended in Buenos Aires (Argentina).

 

At a Glance

Independent sightseeing with some planning. Almeirim is a small, remote Amazon River town rather than a conventional cruise destination. The central waterfront, historic buildings and main squares can be explored on foot, but rainforest and waterfall trips require pre-arranged transport, a local guide and considerably more time.

Getting Ashore

Almeirim has a passenger river terminal on Avenida Beira Rio, close to the town center. However, expedition ships may use tenders or Zodiac boats instead of the local terminal, depending on the vessel, river level and operating conditions. Follow the ship's instructions for the landing point and final return time.

If passengers land near the river terminal, Praça do Centenário is approximately 0.3 km (0.2 mi) away. Much of central Almeirim is walkable, although sidewalks can be uneven and shade is limited. Do not expect a large cruise terminal, organized taxi rank or frequent tourist transport.

Best Ways to Spend the Call

Explore Central Almeirim

Allow 1.5–2.5 hours for an unhurried look at the riverfront and compact town center. The principal sights include Praça do Centenário, the Church of Our Lady of the Conception, Praça do Relógio and several early-20th-century civic buildings. The appeal is the everyday atmosphere of an isolated Amazonian community rather than major monuments.

Walk Along the Amazon Waterfront

The riverfront provides views of local passenger boats, cargo activity and the broad Amazon River. Conditions can change with seasonal flooding, so remain on established streets and paths. Avoid entering working areas or photographing people at close range without permission.

Experience Local Culture and Food

Small shops, markets or temporary fairs may offer regional fruit, fish dishes, snacks and handicrafts. Availability is irregular, and English may be limited. Carry small Brazilian-real notes because cards and foreign currency may not always be accepted.

Take a Ship-Organized Community or Nature Visit

If the cruise program includes a guided community visit, small-boat wildlife outing or forest activity, it will usually be more practical than arranging one after arrival. Local logistics are limited, and independent travelers should not assume that boats, guides or vehicles will be waiting at the landing place.

Self-Guided Walking Tour

Easy Central Almeirim Walk

Distance: approximately 1.5–2 km (0.9–1.2 mi) round trip
Pure walking time: 25–35 minutes
Recommended time: 1.5–2 hours with stops
Difficulty: Easy, but heat, humidity and uneven surfaces can make the walk more tiring.

  1. Passenger landing or river terminal: Begin with views across the Amazon and observe the local river traffic.
  2. Avenida Beira Rio: Follow the central waterfront without entering restricted or working areas.
  3. Praça do Centenário: Walk inland to the town's principal public square, approximately 0.3 km (0.2 mi) from the river terminal.
  4. Church of Our Lady of the Conception: View the parish church and neighboring historic buildings. Interior access depends on whether the church is open.
  5. Historic center: Continue past older civic architecture, including the former municipal building and traditional streets around the center.
  6. Praça do Relógio: Pause at the clock square before returning toward the waterfront.
  7. Return to the landing: Retrace the central streets and allow extra time if the ship is operating tenders.

Street signage may be limited, so save the landing location before starting. Avoid extending the walk into unfamiliar outskirts without a guide.

Trips Beyond Town

The municipality contains rainforest, mountains and waterfalls, including the Panama and Santo Antônio falls, but these are not simple excursions from the Almeirim waterfront. Monte Dourado alone is far from the town and requires a long overland or river transfer. The waterfalls then involve additional boat or road travel.

Organized excursion recommended. Attempt these destinations only when included in a properly arranged full-day program that accounts for river conditions, local transport and the ship's departure. They are unsuitable for an improvised short port call.

Practical Tips

  • Expect high heat and humidity; carry water and use sun protection.
  • Use insect repellent, particularly for guided activities near vegetation or still water.
  • Wear closed, comfortable shoes suitable for uneven or wet ground.
  • Portuguese is the principal language, and English may not be widely spoken.
  • Ask before photographing residents, children, market vendors or private property.
  • Return well before the stated deadline, especially when tenders or Zodiac boats are used.
